societies.name: Ilium (Old-style humans before the service breakdown)
societies.society: The initially serviced old-style human Earth communities

scope.continuity: Simmons Ilium/Olympos continuity, initial Ilium Earth strand
scope.period: The functioning servitor/fax/firmary order before its breakdown
scope.population: Living old-style human residents of the serviced Earth communities
exclusions: Dormant cryogenic intervals counted as active leisure
Later survival settlements assigned the initial service system

societies.description:
The remaining old-style humans receive everyday goods and services from robotic servitors, travel by fax and rely on periodic renewal rather than earning their upkeep. Short accounts describe a predominantly idle population with little knowledge of the machinery supporting it. This is a clear technological separation of basic access from ordinary employment. Security is nevertheless conditional: renewal ends after five twenty-year periods, and the system later fails. The guarantee score covers its functioning period while retaining that severe lifetime limit.

Ordinary residents have little effective command over the productive infrastructure. The short sources do not settle the ultimate mixture of inherited programming, posthuman authority and other actors, so the control coordinate remains unresolved. An autonomous-system regime is provisional, with concentrated external control as an alternative. The high nonworking estimate is a broad reading of the initial population, not a census: exceptional learning, invention and useful exploration still count as work. Once services break down and people must organize their own survival, that later arrangement falls outside this record.

guarantees.basis: Everyday robotic servicing and renewal support a material floor, but the five-twenties limit severely qualifies lifetime security.

control.basis: The serviced humans lack effective control, but short accounts do not resolve the actual controller and its biological or artificial status.

nonworking.basis: Multiple reviews explicitly describe widespread idleness and absence of ordinary labor; allowance remains for exceptional useful learning, invention and exploration. This is an editorial estimate of living residents, not a canonical percentage.

evidence.claim: Robotic service and periodic renewal support the initial Earth population without ordinary jobs, subject to the five-twenties limit.

uncertainties: The controlling intelligence is unresolved; regime 5 is provisional and regime 1 is an alternative by external-control analogy.
The population estimate describes the initial serviced period and is not extended to later survivors.
No whole novel or ending reconstruction was undertaken.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Holy Fire has rations and a post-scarcity interpretation, but its material-production mechanism remains unclear in the short sources.
decisions.analysis: Gerontocratic wealth, medical technology and government support do not alone establish technologically reduced dependence on human production.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; do not turn unequal longevity into an automation economy by itself.

decisions.reason: Rizome is a participatory corporation with working associates, without a verified labor-independent support system.
decisions.analysis: Economic democracy and networked commerce address control, but do not themselves replace human labor as the basis of provision.

decisions.reason: Automated recording and lucrative combat performance do not establish society-wide post-work distribution.
decisions.analysis: The lead is a performance and patronage economy on Reverie. Camera drones do not independently supply ordinary necessities.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; preserve the corrected place name in this disposition.

decisions.reason: The Celestial Kingdom conflict concerns technology and dependence, without a verified distinct post-work arrangement.
decisions.analysis: Resistance to foreign Feed control and development of the Seed are not proof of deliberate job preservation. The Thete public-compiler record cannot be copied to the entire Kingdom.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a technological-sovereignty comparison; skip ending reconstruction.

decisions.reason: The Hegemony's high technology and relationship with the Core do not yet establish a uniform civilian allocation system.
decisions.analysis: Interstellar infrastructure and AI dependence do not resolve labor-independent necessities across the Hegemony worlds. Unhelpful search results are not evidence of absence.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; no import from later Pax institutions.

decisions.reason: The TechnoCore is an AI polity, not by itself a defined human leisure population with a verified support arrangement.
decisions.analysis: Virtual AI activity, human cybrids and separate factions cannot be converted into a human nonworking denominator.

decisions.reason: Ouster/Templar environmental engineering does not resolve member access or the earlier Fall-era economic system.
decisions.analysis: Engineered living space is relevant, but a later Startree description is not a uniform constitution for every earlier Ouster community.

decisions.reason: Pax resurrection and theocratic control do not establish automatic material necessities.
decisions.analysis: Conditional immortality and Core collaboration are separate from an actual labor-independent basic-goods system.

decisions.reason: The initial old-style human population is explicitly supported by robotic servitors without ordinary labor.
Apparent orbital posthuman life does not supply a verified ongoing population and access system in the short check.
decisions.analysis: The initial Earth belief about departed posthumans is not a resolved account of the orbital civilization. Absent or dead people cannot become a leisure rate.
decisions.follow_up: Skip late-plot reconstruction rather than treating the initial premise as final fact.

decisions.reason: Moravecs are active biomechanical persons, but their existence does not establish a post-work economic system or human denominator.
decisions.analysis: Exploration and literary interests are useful activities, not proof of nonwork. No distinct applicable population proxy and distribution mechanism are established.

review_notes: Eleven fast dispositions and one explicit initial-period admission; no novel read or access-denial workaround.
Ilium control remains null rather than assuming every nonhuman or posthuman operator is an AI.
Its nonworking estimate is openly editorial and bounded to the initially serviced living population; the five-twenties limit and later collapse remain visible.
Other cybernetic, medical and astroengineering settings retain explicit material-economy gaps.
